equity_bridge.item: H1 2026 unlevered owner FCF already distributed (vintage alignment: 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet vs FY2026 year-1 flows)
equity_bridge.note: Q2 2026 report: H1 OCF 2,876 - property additions 1,134 - SBC 68 + after-tax interest paid (503 x 0.75 = 377). Deducted so the FY2026 flow is not credited twice against a balance sheet that already reflects its payout.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (FY2020-FY2025, 4.6%) tempered toward management's FY2026 frame of low-single-digit RTM growth plus ~3% core pricing; equity CAGR rejected as the primary because C$2-4.7B/yr of buybacks shrink book equity regardless of earnings power
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR (1.9%) diverges >30% from revenue (4.6%) and EPS (8.6%) CAGRs. Structural, not a data error: CN retires 2-4% of its shares a year with debt-funded buybacks, so book equity is flat while per-share metrics compound. 3-yr CAGRs from FY2022 are ~0 across the board because FY2022 was a pricing/fuel-surcharge peak (freight revenue per RTM 7.03c) and FY2023-24 absorbed wildfires, the 2024 lockout and a tariff-driven volume slump.
historical_growth.notes: All CAGRs computed on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; interest income nil). Start points FY2020 and FY2022 chosen because FY2017 (US tax-reform gain), FY2021 (C$886M KCS break fee inside OCF and net income) and FY2023 (deferred-tax recovery) are distorted. Owner-FCF 3-yr CAGR of -5.2% versus EBITDA -0.2% and revenue +0.4% is capex, not SBC: property additions rose from 2,750 (FY2022) to 3,658 (FY2025) in the second capacity surge; SBC is 0.4-0.6% of revenue throughout and is not the driver. FY2021 reported FCF of 4,080 is ~3,200 ex break fee.

scenario_narratives.base: CN compounds revenue at 3-4% (low-single-digit volumes, ~3% core pricing) with the operating ratio returning to ~61.5% from the FY2026 inflation-hit 62.5%, capex normalising at ~18% of revenue after the guided 2026 trough, and cash taxes converging on the 24% book rate as accelerated depreciation unwinds. Buybacks keep the share count flat and are value-neutral; the dividend (C$3.66/yr) is funded from the modelled flows.
scenario_narratives.bull: Transpacific (Prince Rupert) and Gulf Coast energy/petrochemical volumes plus modal share gains from trucking lift RTM growth to mid-single digits; tariff disputes settle; PSR takes the OR back below 60% (EBITDA margin 52%); capex settles at 17% with the capacity programs complete.
scenario_narratives.bear: Tariff recession in 2027 plus a labour stoppage at the TCRC contract expiry and grain mean-reversion push revenue down ~1% in 2027 and the OR to 64-65%; the UP-NS merger weakens CN's US interline position; capex stays elevated at 19%; growth resets to 2%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: An irreplaceable, regulated-duopoly network asset with ~50% EBITDA margins and a 30-year dividend record, valued on fully-SBC-expensed unlevered owner FCF at a CAD-built 7.5% WACC with the terminal value capped at 20x FCF. CN trades at ~37x trailing FCF and ~14.5x EV/EBITDA, i.e. the market discounts it at something closer to 6-6.5%; the house model does not grant that rate, so the stock screens as a quality asset at a full price rather than a mispricing. The required-return table is the honest read: at today's price the implied return is well below the 15% hurdle.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: value is terminal-heavy and long-duration; each 0.5pp on WACC moves base value ~10%. The 20x cap binds at 7.5%/2.5% so terminal growth sensitivity is muted but WACC sensitivity is not.
Capex normalisation: the base assumes 18% of revenue long-run vs 15.4% guided for 2026 and ~21% averaged over 2017-25; each 1pp of revenue in perpetual capex is ~C$9-10/share.
Cash tax: ramped to 24% vs 14-20% actual; if accelerated depreciation remains a structural shelter the base understates value by ~C$8-10/share.
Pension surplus (~C$5.4B asset, ~C$6/share after tax) deliberately excluded from the bridge; an upside if ever accessible.
Tariff/trade policy, TCRC contract expiry Dec-2026, and the UP-NS merger are the bear-case triggers; the grain MRE caps pricing on ~22% of revenue.
Half-year vintage: year-1 is the full FY2026 against a 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet; corrected via the -C$2,050M equity_bridge item. At the FY2026 annual update, drop that item and roll FY0 to FY2026.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report Note 19, total stock-based compensation expense C$106M (Share Units 64 + VIDP 1 + options 11 + ESIP 30); CN publishes no separate equity-award tax line, net-share settlement is immaterial (options/ESIP settled by share trusts)
inputs.share_count_basis: 604.9M common shares issued at 30-Jun-2026 (Q2 2026 equity statement, includes 1.1M held in Share Trusts, treated as outstanding) plus 1.0M dilutive effect of stock-based compensation (Q2 2026 Note 7) = 605.9M fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, so grant dilution is already charged; buybacks (C$2.06B FY2025, C$1.34B H1 2026, 24M-share NCIB to Feb-2027) are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Current portion of long-term debt 512 + Long-term debt 21,742 = 22,254 less cash and cash equivalents 280 (restricted cash 14 excluded) = 21,974 at 30-Jun-2026. Operating lease liabilities (465) EXCLUDED, see lease_treatment. Pension plans in deficiency (337) excluded and the C$5.4B pension asset on the other side also excluded, see notes.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CAD, the currency of the flows. Risk-free: Government of Canada 10-year ~3.5% (Oct 2026). ERP 5.0%, beta 0.9 (Class I rails, 5-yr monthly vs S&P/TSX) -> cost of equity 8.0%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.6% (FY2025 interest 913 on ~21B average debt = 4.3%, recent issues ~4.5-5%), after tax at 24.5% = 3.5%. Market weights: equity 101.8B (168.06 x 605.9M) vs debt 22.3B -> D/V 18%. WACC = 0.82 x 8.0 + 0.18 x 3.5 = 7.2%, carried at 7.5% in all three scenarios. The 0.3pp rounding is the only margin applied in the discount rate; scenario risk (tariffs, labour, grain cycle, UP-NS) is in the flows and the weights, not stacked on WACC, and WACC is identical across scenarios (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. CN reports under US GAAP: operating lease cost (~C$100M/yr) is inside operating expenses, so the reported operating ratio and EBITDA are already after lease cost and lease payments are in operating cash flow. Operating lease liabilities (C$465M incl. current at 30-Jun-2026) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt; lease_cost_pct_path is 0 because the charge is already inside ebitda_margin_path. CN has no material finance leases.
inputs.nci_treatment: None. CN has no non-controlling interests; net income is 100% attributable.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: operating company, non-US/cyclical row -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations (a1) CAD WACC, (b) lease treatment, (f) risk charged once). Not a bank/REIT/LIC. First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. BASE YEAR: FY2025 (Dec year end) is the FY0 revenue the growth path compounds from; FY2025 is a clean year (no one-offs; adj EPS 7.63 vs reported 7.57). FY2017 (US tax-reform deferred-tax gain, Q4 NI 2,611), FY2021 (KCS merger break fee ~C$886M net in Q3 OCF/NI) and FY2023 (Q4 deferred-tax recovery, NI 2,130) are distorted and are NOT used as base years or as CAGR endpoints; growth rates below use FY2020 and FY2022 as start points and EBITDA/adjusted EPS as the normalised series. VINTAGE: balance sheet and share count are 30-Jun-2026 (latest filing) while the projection's year 1 is the full FY2026, so H1 2026 unlevered owner FCF (OCF 2,876 - property additions 1,134 - SBC 68 + after-tax interest paid 503 x 0.75 = ~2,050) has already been paid out as dividends (1,112) and buybacks (1,337) and is reflected in the June net debt and share count; it is deducted once in equity_bridge to avoid crediting it twice. FCF BASIS: reported_fcf 3,391 = FY2025 OCF 7,049 - property additions 3,658 (CSV convention; CN's own FCF definition incl. other investing items is 3,336). last_fcf = 3,391 - 106 SBC - 0 interest income = 3,285 (levered, post-interest, as the history requires). The projected flows are UNLEVERED (EBITDA - SBC - D&A -> cash tax -> + D&A - capex +/- WC), so year-1 projected FCF (~4.6B) exceeds last_fcf by the after-tax interest (~0.7B) plus the guided capex step-down (FY2026 program C$2.8B net vs C$3.66B gross additions in FY2025). INTEREST INCOME: 0, CN is a net debtor; no stripping. PENSION: CN's main Canadian plan is in surplus (pension asset C$5,362M at 31-Dec-2025 against C$337M of plans in deficiency). The C$502M/yr 'Other components of net periodic benefit income' sits BELOW operating income and is NOT in ebitda_margin_path, so the income is stripped; the matching asset is deliberately NOT added to the bridge because surplus access is restricted under Canadian pension legislation and the realised benefit (contribution holidays on the main plan) already shows up as cash pension contributions far below the service cost expensed in EBITDA. This is a conservative, unmodelled upside of roughly C$3.7B after tax (~C$6/share) if the surplus were ever accessible. TAX: cash taxes FY2025 935 on EBIT 6,593 = 14%, FY2022-24 18-20%, H1 2026 ~20%, versus a ~24.5% blended statutory/book rate; the gap is accelerated tax depreciation (Canadian AII, US bonus depreciation) which persists while capex exceeds D&A. The cash rate is ramped from 19% to 24% by year 7 rather than perpetuating the shelter. CAPEX: FY2026 guidance C$2.8B net (~15.4% of revenue); 2017-2025 gross additions averaged ~21% of revenue including two capacity surges. The base path steps from 15.5% back to 18% because the 2026 level is a post-surge trough, not a run-rate. WORKING CAPITAL: wc_capture -3% (receivables grow with freight revenue; CN's WC changes are small). SBC: 0.6% of revenue, held flat; house/street band is narrow.

bear.narrative: A tariff-driven North American industrial recession in 2027 cuts cross-border autos, metals and forest products while the 2026/27 grain crop reverts to the five-year average; the TCRC contract expiring 31-Dec-2026 produces another stoppage; the UP-NS merger reshapes US interline economics against CN's southern traffic. Operating ratio drifts to 64-65% (EBITDA margin 46.5-47.5%) under wage and fuel inflation CN cannot fully pass through under the grain MRE; capex stays at 19% to fund resilience after wildfire/washout disruptions; long-run growth 2%.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue +5.5% (H1 +5.3% with Q2 +11% on record grain, CAD at 0.71 and soft Q3-Q4 2025 comps; guidance raised to low-single-digit RTM growth, mid-to-high single-digit adjusted EPS growth). Thereafter low-single-digit RTM growth plus ~3% pricing, fading to 2.5% nominal. EBITDA margin from 48.5% (FY2026 OR ~62.5% incl. fuel and wage inflation) back to 50% (OR ~61.5%, where CN sat in FY2025) and no further: the 2022 sub-60 OR is treated as a pricing-peak outcome, not the run-rate. Capex steps up from the guided 15.5% trough to 18%, cash tax ramps to 24%.

bull.narrative: Prince Rupert and Gulf Coast volumes (transpacific intermodal, LNG/petrochemicals) plus continued trucking share gains lift RTMs to mid-single digits for several years; tariff disputes resolve without a structural hit to cross-border autos/metals; PSR execution takes the operating ratio back under 60% as it was in 2022, so EBITDA margin reaches 52%; capex normalises at 17% because the Western Canada double-tracking and Prince Rupert corridor builds are complete; accelerated depreciation keeps the cash tax rate at 23%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% house default): three live, independent 2026-27 risks named by management -- US-Canada tariff policy on cross-border autos/metals/forest products, the TCRC labour contract expiring 31-Dec-2026 after the 2024 lockout, and the pending UP-NS merger -- any one of which produces the bear path. Base 50%. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): the bull case needs both mid-single-digit volume growth AND a sub-60% OR, and CN has not held both together since 2022; the 30% reflects that the moat makes the base case robust but the upside is capped by a mature, regulated volume base.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
